title: Socinus and his followers deny that God has certain foreknowledge of future contingents
source_text: THESIS I. SOCINUS & ejus asseclae intelligere non valentes, qua ratione certo praescire possint futura contingentia, & quae non habent causam necessariam & determinatam, ejusmodi futurorum certam praescientiam in ipso Deo dari negant.
pass_a_gloss: THESIS I. SOCINUS and his followers not being able to understand, by what reason future contingents can be certainly foreknown, and things which have not a necessary and determinate cause, deny that a certain foreknowledge of futures of this kind is given in God himself.
pass_b_english: Socinus and his followers cannot understand how future contingents, things that have no necessary and determinate cause, can be known in advance with certainty.
They therefore deny that God himself has any certain foreknowledge of future events of this kind.

choices.why: The Schools' term for future events without a necessary and determinate cause; kept as a technical term.
